GENERAL RECOMMENDATIONS 

  Besides the specific recommendations made in  the previous paras, the Committee desires 
that the Government should also address the following problems of the UT of Daman & Diu: 
(i) The main sources of livelihood of D&D are Fisheries and Tourism. Some 
development activities like Distillery in Daman, have come up but the main economic 
activity is coastal tourism on which a s ubstantial part of the population survives. 
D&D is one of the most beautiful Union Territories in the country with vast sandy 
beaches and non-polluted coastal waters. The Committee recommends that the 
tourism potential of this Union Territory ha rnessed fully, so that tourists visit in 
large numbers to the UT and the means of livelihood of its residents multiply with 
the income generated from the proceeds of tourism. Steps should also be taken for 
encouraging the opening of resorts and hotels in the UT. 
(ii) One of the main reasons affecting the economic developm ent of D&D is the existing 
Coastal Regulation Zone Notification, 1991, which is very restrictive in nature. As 
57% of land is covered under Coastal Regulati on Zone, this notification has affected 
the livelihood of the fishermen communities including construction of their dwelling 
units apart from affecting the developm ent of coastal tour ism. The Committee 
understands that the Ministry of Environment and Forests is in the process of 
amending the Coastal Regulation Zone No tification, 1991 and trying to make a 
region specific notification on the lines of Prof. M.S. Swaminathan Committee 
Report. Necessary steps are required to be taken for removing the restrictions in the 
existing Coastal Regulation Zone for the promotion of tourism sector. 
(iii) The UT Administration had proposed construction of New bridges between Nani 
Daman and Moti Dama n and between Diu and mainla nd Gujarat. A few of the 
projects have been technically approve d by the Ministry of Shipping, Road 
Transport and Highways in June 2009 but the same have not seen the light of the 
day. Their financial approval is pending in the MHA. The Committee recommends 
that the Ministry of Home Affairs should expedite the approval so that the long 
pending demands of both Daman and Diu are taken care of at the earliest. 
(iv) The Committee was informed that the 51s t Battalion of the India Reserve Battalion, 
with headquarters in the UT of Lakshadw eep, has a very peculiar instance on the 
recruitment policy. The recruits to this Battalion cater to the needs of the UTs of 
D&D, DNH and Lakshadweep. The recruitment to this Battalion is from these three 
UTs. However these recruits are posted for a total period of four years away from 
their native place causing a lot of hardship, mainly due to the language problem. The 
Committee feels that the local recruits should stay within their Territory which will 
help them to lead a better family life  and thereby improve their operational 
efficiency. 
(v) The Committee has been apprised that the discharge of effluents (mostly untreated) 
from the chemical units in the GIDC Estate of Vapi into Daman Ganga River leads 
to contamination of the river and the polluted water flows through Daman emitting a 
lot of foul smell. Most of the potable water in Daman, which is ground water, gets 
contaminated due to seepage of the pollut ed water. Coastal Marine life and tourist 

spots are adversely affected. The Commi ttee feels that the problem needs to 
addressed urgently which if allowed to continue may lead to drop in revenue earning 
as the tourists have already started moving away from the coastal areas of D&D. 
(vi) The Committee, notes that both Daman and Diu depend on the Gujarat Government 
for water supply, which at present is not sufficient. Therefore, the Committee 
recommends that additional allocati on from Madhuban Da m for Daman and 
Narmada Canal for Diu has to be considered at the earliest. 
(vii) The UT of D & D does not produce elec tricity and are dependent on NTPC and the 
Western Grid for their requirement. A solu tion to the demand-supply gap has to be 
filled in at the earliest so that the existing industrial units are not forced to shift base. 
(viii) To improve health care,  a Government or Governme nt sponsored Super Speciality 
Hospital is the need of the hour for Diu and should be considered on top priority, 
(ix) More incentives to industrial houses to set up units in Da man and Diu to help 
generate employment for the locals and al so to generate revenue for the UT, may 
also be considered. 
(Para 5.16.1) 
CLARIFICATIONS SOUGHT IN RESPECT OF UTs OF DADRA & NAGAR HAVELI AND 
DAMAN AND DIU 
  The information as forwarded by the Minist ry of Home Affairs has been perused. While 
information in respect of tax and duty evasion ca ses and in respect of some other items in the 
two UTs in the first quarter of 2010 have been furnished as directed by the Committee, certain 
interesting aspects emerged therefro m. Initially the Ministry of Home Affairs sought a month’s 
time to compile the information as it was voluminous in nature and was to be compiled from 
different Ministries and agencies, but in replies to many of the questions, it has now been stated 
that the requisite information may be collected from the Mini stry of Finance (Customs and 
Excise Department) and the Ministry of Commerce. In respect of some other questions one 
month’s time has again been sought  for submission of replies on th e plea that the material to be 
collected would be voluminous. It has further been found that in respect of those questions 
where time has been sought to reply, the administ rations of the two UTs have already furnished 
voluminous information to the Committee.  
(Para 5.17.5) 
  At the outset, the Committee would like to observe that as per established practice, 
whenever, it requires any informat ion, the concerned Ministry und er its jurisdiction is asked to 
supply the same irrespective of the fact that the informatio n may concern other Ministry, 
Department or State Government. It is perhaps the first time, in the history of the Committee 
that the administrative Ministry  concerned is asking it to pr ocure the requisite information 
from other Ministries directly. In the same vein, the Ministry is also seeking extension of time 
for supply of material in respect  of certain other questions. While  information has already been 
furnished by UT Administrations, the Committee takes a serious note of the casual approach of 
the Ministry of Home Affairs and the Administrator in respo nding to the request of the 
Standing Committee. The Committee therefore direc ts the Ministry and the Administrator to 

supply the requisite information to it positively within fifteen days  from the presentation of the 
Report. (Para 5.17.6) 
  In reply to the query of the Committee regardi ng instances of evasion of taxes and duties, 
if any, by enterprises, including violations of the Goa, Daman & Diu Excise Duty Act and Rules, 
1964 detected year-wise since 2004-05 by the Da man and Diu Administrati on and others, cases 
registered etc., the UT administration has prov ided incomplete and contradictory information 
instead of facilitating the Committ ee to understand the ground realitie s, particularly relating to 
the level of alertness of the concerned Depart ments in ensuring collection of Government 
revenue commensurating with th e business activities of the units operating from the Union 
Territories of Daman & Diu and Dadra & Nagar Haveli. (Para 5.17.7) 
  For instance, the volume of Excise Duty coll ection is stated to have “more than doubled” 
since 2004-05, from 24.24 crore to Rs. 57.90 crore, but the reply is silent about what this increase 
in collection of Excise Duty has been attr ibutable to. It was incumbent upon the UT 
Administration to explain as to whether the incr ease in Excise Duty collection every year was 
due to enhanced volume of production by the units, or revision of rates or for any other reasons, 
to enable the Committee to und erstand the ground situation. By  providing such incomplete 
information, the Committee has been denied that opportunity. (Para 5.17.8) 
  More glaring in the reply is the attempt of  providing contradictory information to the 
Committee. While, on the one hand, it  is stated in the reply that “no evasion of Excise Duty has 
been detected during the period in  question” on the other hand it is  stated “...... recently during the 
meetings of the Joint Regional Intelligence sharing, apprehensions have been raised regarding 
probable evasion of the excise duty by the distilleries in Daman” and that “.......In the interest of the 
Government revenue, the Department has moved swif tly and only on the apprehensions of the 
excise duty evasion the show cause notices have been issued to the Distilleries of Daman as to why 
the excise duty of Rs. 300 crores ( approximately. total of all distilleries) should not be raised upon 
them for last five years.” It is fu rther stated that, “......notices have been issued just to pre-empt any 
time barring of the demand in case the raising of demand found justified and also as apprehensions 
were raised”. 
  The Committee, it appears, is  being sought to be kept in th e dark as to the genesis of the 
“apprehension” leading to issuance of notices for recovery of ev aded Excise Duty for periods 
covering past five years. Whether the said Jo int Regional Intelligence has been exercising 
surveillance over the region encompassing Gujarat, Goa, Maha rashtra, besides the UTs of 
Daman & Diu and Dadra & Nagar Haveli, and had pi cked up clues leading to the conceiving of 
“apprehensions” about the alleged evasion of Excise Duty by distilleries operating in Daman? In

(Paras 5.17.9 & 5.17.10) 
  Moreover, it remains unclear as to how th e UT Administration could issue notices for 
recovery of Excise Duty to assessees simply based on “apprehension” that it had been evaded for 
the past five years. Does it not weaken the case and strengthen the alleged taxes/duty evaders to 
challenge the demands of the Department in the Court? 

  It should be incumbent upon  Government to ascertain the facts of the above developments 
with particular reference to the questions raised  by the Committee, as above, and enlighten the 
Committee about the ground realities of the matter. (Para 5.17.11 and 5.17.12) 
CENSUS 2011 AND NATIONAL POPULATION REGISTER 
  The Committee takes into account the deta iled arrangements made for Census 2011, 
formation of UIDAI for issuance of Unique Identi fication Number and compilation of National 
Population Register (NPR). The Committee unders tands that Census of the country is a 
cumbersome process. However, it is significant in view of the fact that all the policies, 
programmes and schemes of the Government are fr amed on the basis of the conclusions drawn 
from the Census. (Para 6.9.1) 
  The Committee observes that the first phase  of the Census 2011 will be held during April 
and September 2010 for collection of data on Ho uselisting & Housing Census as well as for 
preparation of National Population Register. The Committee apprehends that it will be difficult 
and improper to carry out both exercises together for the following reasons: 
(i) The Census information is collected u nder the Census Act, 1948 which guarantees 
complete confidentiality of  the individual and household data collected. This 
confidentiality clause is known to be a ke y-stone that ensures accuracy and sanctity 
of the Census Data; and 
(ii) The National Population Register (NPR) information is to be collected under the 
Citizenship Act, 1955 read with the Citi zenship (Registration and Issue of National 
Identity Cards) Rules, 2003 and the data collected are not confidential and are meant 
to be used for identifying individuals and household. Thes e make the purpose, 
objectives and the process of the two exercise different and, hence, it is important to 
keep the two exercises separate in order to maintain sanctity of both. (Para 6.9.2) 
  With regard to the confidentiality of the Census Data, the Committee apprehends that it 
would be difficult to hold back information contained in the Census Schedule in view of the RTI 
Act, 2005. It is quite likely that even if exem ption clause is invoked under RTI Act, 2005, the 
CIC, the Supreme Court or the High Courts may pass orders for disclosure of information. The 
Committee therefore recommends to Government to keep this aspect in mind. (Para 6.9.3) 
  The Committee also took note of the statemen t made by the Ministry of Home Affairs that 
the creation of National Population Register would be a comprehensive identity database in the 
country for better targeting of the benefits and services under the Government 
schemes/programmes, improving planning and strengthening securi ty of the country. However, 
the Committee is of the considered view that the ‘Nationality As  Declared’ clause in the NPR 
Household Schedule has the potential to confer de facto Indian Citizenship to illegal migrants, 
despite the disclaimer attached  to the clause. The Committee is of the opinion that the 
Government should not act in haste. There is a need to have a rethinking on the NPR exercise. 
The Committee, therefore, strongly recommends th at the ‘Nationality’ clause should be 
removed as it has the potents in the long run which may pose a threat to the security and 
integrity of the country. Therefo re, it may be worthwhile cons idering suspension of the NPR 

exercise for the time being. The Committee fu rther recommends that th e work relating to NPR 
preparation should be de-linked from the Census operations. (Para 6.9.4) 
HOUSING SCHEME FOR DELHI POLICE 
  The Committee is constrained to note that  there is undue delay in allocating land for 
housing projects by the DDA. Being a Government organization, DDA should not function on 
purely commercial lines like private builders. The Committee recommends that DDA should 
make more concerted efforts to acquire land exclusively for police housing of Delhi Police so 
that the pressing need of the police personnel could be met. Keeping in mind the sensitive law 
and order situation in Delhi, proper functioning of Police Stations and keeping the morale of the 
police force high are of utmost importance. Therefore, making land available for Police Stations 
and Housing Projects, requires immediate attention of the authorities. The Committee therefore 
urges upon the DDA, , MCD and other agencies to make land available for Housing projects and 
Police Stations in Delhi with least delay.  
(Para 7.7.1) 
To achieve 40% satisfaction level, Delhi Police needs a total of about 28,000 houses against about 
15,000 houses available with it, thus, leaving a gap of about 13,000 quarters. The Committee is 
concerned that by 2012-13 only about 7,000 flats are likely to be added, including the projects 
under PPP model. This is grossly inadequate. Co nsidering the rate at which the quarters are 
being constructed and that additional land is not available with Delhi Police, the target can only 
be achieved in a reasonable period by outrig ht purchase of ready built flats from DDA. The 
Committee is of the view that the Ministry of Home Affairs should take  up the matter of ready 
built flats for Delhi Police with DDA and the D DA on its part should also make provision for 
500-550 flats every year for Delhi Police.   
  The Committee feels that on the one hand De lhi Police faces scarcity of Housing for its 
personnel and on the other the fu nds allocated, particularly non- plan allocation, are not spent 
fully. During 2006-07 only a fraction was spent where as in 2007-08 and 2008-09, more than 10 
per cent could not be spent. For achieving physi cal targets, achieving financial targets is 
necessary. Delhi Police should take necessary steps to achieve financial targets. (Para 7.7.3) 
  The Committee is of the view that police bu ildings should be decl ared as operational 
buildings as has been done in the case of Railways and P & T so that construction could start 
straightaway. The Committee is also of the view that the average time  taken for declaring 
buildings as operational should also be brought down so as to expedite the process. (Para 7.7.4) 
  The Committee feels that for achieving 40 per cent satisfaction level,  present allocations - 
both Plan and Non-Plan - are not sufficient. Government should therefore assess the total 
requirement of funds. Allocations should be increased to enable Delhi Police to achieve desired 
satisfaction within the next five years. (Para 7.7.5) 
  The Committee does not understand why Delh i Police makes such a target which cannot 
be achieved. During tenth plan 40% satisfaction level was proposed and only 22.91 % was 
achieved. Again 40% is being proposed for Eleven th Plan. This is not a right approach. Delhi 
Police should try to keep realistic targets only. (Para 7.7.6) 

  The Committee desires that the pitfalls of the Tenth Plan have to be avoided and the 
physical targets fixed for the eleventh Five-Y ear Plan should be achieved. Clearance of 
proposals and clearance for lands may be taken up at the highest level so that these areas do not 
act as impediments for the achievement of targets. (Para 7.7.7) 
  In the non-plan scheme also, things are not moving in the right direction. Out of 17 PS 
buildings, only 3 were expected to be ready by 31.3.2010 and out of 1,4 81 staff quarters, 13 were 
expected by ready by 31.3.2010. This needs to be  looked into and steps may be taken for timely 
completion of the buildings and quarters. (Para 7.7.8) 
  It is a welcome step that about 5,202 quarters are proposed to be constructed under Public 
Private Partnership (PPP) model at Dheerpur and Police Headquarters are proposed to be 
constructed at Parliament Street . As mentioned in the Outcome Budget, the financial mode for 
the projects may be finalized quickly. All other st eps may also be taken to ensure that both the 
projects are completed by 2013.   
  All the projects, which are under way in both Plan and Non-Plan Schemes, may be 
completed as per the targets and there should not be any cost and time over-runs. (Para 7.7.10) 
  The Committee was given to understand that one of the reasons for the shortfall in the 
housing project was non-completion of constr uction by PWD in time. The Committee takes 
strong exception to this. If PWD does not impr ove its performance, Delhi Police may go in for 
construction by other public sector undertakings. (Para 7.7.11) 
  The Committee appreciates that a Proj ect Monitoring Committee (PMC) under the 
Chairmanship of Joint Secretary (UT), Ministry of Home Affairs has been set up to monitor the 
building plans of Delhi Police. The Committee de sires that this Committee should strictly 
monitor the implementation on a regular basis and ensure that the projects are completed in 
time. 
(Para 7.7.12) 
HOUSING SCHEME FOR CENTRAL POLICE FORCES 
  The Committee observes that just a little mo re than 15% of the Force personnel entitled to 
family accommodation, are able to avail the fac ility. Force personnel, who remain deployed at 
international borders as well as in violence infested regions, are engaged in grappling with 
militancy and insurgency throughout the year. They do not even have the mental comfort of 
their families having proper accommodation, medi cal facilities etc, while they are away from 
home. 
(Para 7.17.1) 
  The Committee taking note of the findings of  the BPR&D study feels that the Scheme is 
beneficial and recommends that it should be continued. (Para 7.17.2 
  The Committee takes a serious note of the fact that the deficiency of the housing units as 
on 1.4.1009 was 114634. If the new battalions, which had been approved by the Government and 
were likely to be raised by 201 3-14 were also taken into ac count, forty thousand personnel 
would be further added. The allocations have been made as per the current requirements only. 
As this rate, the gap would keep on increasing and it would be a never ending phenomenon. The 

Committee agrees that the allocations have not kept pace with the increase in number of 
personnel in various Central Police Forces and this situation is likely to go from bad to worse. 
The Committee therefore recommends that the Government should seriously assess the financial 
requirements for the housing of the CPF personne l. The Ministry informed the Committee that 
due to massive housing shortage, the funds were in adequate and they would move for additional 
funds at RE stage. The Committee suggests that a dditional funds may be sought at RE 2010-11 
stage. (Para 7.17.3) 
  The Committee recommends that to supplemen t the funds requirement, not covered by 
the Planning Commission, Ministry  of Finance may be allowed to make adequate allocation 
from the ‘Non-Plan’ side also so as to enable the forces to meet the housing requirements.(Para 7.17.4) 
  The CPFs are facing the problem of land acquisition for construction of houses. The 
responsibility of acquiring land lies with the Stat e Governments and a lot of time is taken for 
completing the acquisition process. This area needs to be addressed. The Committee desires that 
the Home Secretary may address the Chief Secretar ies of all the State Governments about the 
necessity of early clearances for the land acquisition. (Para 7.17.5) 
  The construction of houses for CPFs also su ffers due to problems of capacity utilization of 
the implementing agencies. The Committee ther efore suggests that besides CPWD, more and 
more public sector agencies may be considered for executing the projects. (Para 7.17.6) 
  The Ministry proposed to launch a mega housing project for CPFs to address problems of 
accommodation for the forces personnel on Public Private Partnership basis. The Committee 
desires that an early decision may be taken in this regard. (Para 7.17.7) 
  The Committee appreciates the amendment made in Rule 126 of GFR allowing the 
involvement of other Public Works Organisati ons as the same would help in avoiding 
unnecessary delays and other regulatory bottlen ecks in completion of housing projects for 
Central Police Forces in time. However, the purpo se will be defeated if there are inordinate 
delays in giving nod/concurrence. The Committee, therefore recommends that a reasonable time 
limit should be imposed in giving clearance by Ministry of Urban Development/CPWD. The 
Committee also recommends that Engineering Wing s of CPFs be further strengthened so that 
they can be entrusted more project works for spee ding construction of residential as well as 
other type of accommodation. (Para 7.17.8) 
  A well approach coordinated is needed amon gst various agencies so that the regulatory 
and logistic requirements are me t well before the projects are given a go-ahead and that the 
projects do not get stuck at the implementation stage due to procedural hurdles. Clearances from  
local bodies through an institutionalized  mechanism, with all-round support from the clearance 
agencies should be done on fast track basis. (Para 7.17.9)

3.0  The Chair then invited the Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India to make a 
presentation on Census, 2011 and the National Population Register. 
3.1  The Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India made a powerpoint presentation. 
After the presentation, the Chairman and the members of the Committee raised following issues and 
queries:--- 
z It would be difficult to hold back information contained in the Census Schedule: in view 
of the RTI Act, 2005. It is quite likely that even if exemption clause is invoked under RTI 
Act, 2005, the CIC, the Supreme Court or the High Courts may pass orders for disclosure 
of information. The Committee therefore recommended to Government to keep this aspect 
in mind. 

z The Ministry of Home Affairs maintained that the creation of National Population 
Register would be a comprehensive identity database in the country, for better targeting of 
the benefits and services under the Government Schemes/Programmes, improving 
planning and strengthening security of the country. Therefore, the ‘Nationality As 
Declared’ clause in the NPR Household Schedule has the potential to confer de facto  
Indian Citizenship to illegal migrants, despite the disclaimer attached to the clause. 
z The Government should not act in haste. There is a need to have a rethinking on the NPR 
exercise and the ‘Nationality’ clause should be removed as it has the potents in the long 
run which may pose a threat to the security a nd integrity of the country. Therefore, it may 
be worthwhile considering suspension of th e NPR exercise for the time being. Besides, 
the work relating to NPR preparation should be de-linked from the Census operations.

PREFACE 
 
 I, the Chairman of the Department-re lated Parliamentary Standing Committee on 
Home Affairs, having been authorized by the Committee to submit the report on its 
behalf, do hereby present this One-Hundred  and Forty Fifth Report on Demands for 
Grants (2010-11) relating to the Ministry  of Development of North Eastern Region 
(DoNER).  
2. Under Rule 272  of the Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business in the Council 
of States, the Department-rela ted Parliamentary Standing Co mmittee on Home Affairs is 
mandated to consider the Demands for Grants of the related Ministries, and make report 
theron. In pursuance thereof, the Committee heard the presentation of the concerned 
Secretary, DoNER and other officials of the Ministry, in its sitting held on 5th April, 2010 
and examined the Demands for Grants (2010-11) of that Ministry..  
3. The Committee considered and adopte d the Report in its sitting held on 4
th May, 
2010. 
4. The Committee, while making its obs ervations/recommendations, has relied 
mainly upon the following papers received from the Ministry of DoNER: -

Chapter - I 
 
OVERVIEW 
 
1.1.1 The North-Eastern part of India comprise s of the States of Arunachal Pradesh, 
Assam, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Naga land, Sikkim and Tripur a. Flanked by lofty 
hills, the mighty Brahmaputra river slashes a central path between its north and south.  
The western side of the North East is conn ected to the eastern part of the Indian 
subcontinent by a narrow land corridor, sometim es referred to as the Siliguri Neck or 
"Chicken's Neck". The NER of India covers an area of 2.62 lakh s q. km. It accounts for 
7.9% of total geographical area of the c ountry. With a total population of 39 million 
(2001), it accounts for 3.8% of total population of India.  The entire North-East of India 
is marked by diversity in customs, culture s, traditions and languages and a home to 
multifarious social, ethnic and linguistic groups.   
 
1.1.2 Richly endowed with natural resources, India's North Eastern Region is a rainbow 
area; extraordinarily diverse and colourful.  The region is one of the biodiversity hotspots 
in the world, and it has the highest rainfall in the country, with large and small river 
systems nesting the land and is a treasur e house of flora and fauna.  Another unique 
strength of the region in the present era of globalization, and in th e context of India's 
Look East Policy, is its long international bor ders.  Despite having hilly and inhospitable 
terrains, porous borders, highl y inadequate connectivity, limited air services, inadequate 
rail links and weak telecommunication infrastr ucture, the NE Region has the potential to 
become India’s most attractive place and most sought after tourist destination.   
 
1.1.3 According to the Ministry of DoNER, rapid development of the NER is among 
the foremost priorities of the Central Government.  In view of their strategic significance, 
the States of the region have been accorded th e status of Special Category States.  With 
an objective to fast track economic growth of  the region, the Department of North East 
Region was formed in September 2001 which was upgraded to the status of a Ministry in 
2004 to push further socio-economic developmen t of the region. This Ministry, rather 
than an administrative unit, acts as  a facilitator be tween the Central 
Minisries/Departments and the State Govern ments of the North Eastern Region for 
economic development including removal of in frastructural bottlen ecks, provision of 
basic minimum services, creating an environm ent for private investment and to remove 
impediments to lasting peace and security in the region. 
 
1.1.4 The Ministry of Development of Nort h Eastern Region seeks to achieve the 
following goals: 
 
(i) Accelerating the pace of socio-economic development in the  
 North Eastern Region; 
 
(ii) Synergizing the efforts of Central/State Governments/Other

account the heightened consciousness of the people of the  region,

(v) Formulating appropriate policies for the rapid development of

1.2 NON-LAPSABLE CENTRAL PO OL OF RESOURCES FOR NORTH 
EASTERN REGION (NLCPR) 
1.2.1 The North East has essentially b een dependent on central funding for 
development works. All the States in th e NER are Special Category States, whose 
development plans are centrally financed on the basis of 90% Grant and 10% Loan. 
Further, the Special Category States are allowed to use up to 20% of the central 
assistance for Non-plan expenditure. 
1.2.2  As the benefits of economic developm ent have yet to steadily accrue to the 
region, efforts have been ini tiated in this dire ction through various supportive measures. 
In October 1996, the then Prime Minister anno unced "New Initiatives for North Eastern 
 8

Region" and stipulated that at least 10% of the Budget(s) of the Central 
Ministries/Departments will be earmarked for the development of North Eastern States. A 
preliminary exercise undertaken by the Planning Commission revealed that the 
expenditure on the North East by some Uni on Ministries during 1997-98 fell short of the 
stipulated 10% of the Gross Budgetary  Support (GBS) for that year. Planning 
Commission thereafter explored the possibility of creating a Central Pool of Resources 
for the North East out of the unspent amount of stipulated 10% of GBS to support 
infrastructure development projects in the North East.   
1.2.3 Since 1998-99, all non-exempted Ministries/D epartments of Government of India 
are required to earmark at least 10% of th eir GBS for the development of North Eastern 
States for creation of both economic and social  infrastructure such as power, roads and 
bridges, education, health, water supply and sanitation, etc. in the region.  The unutilized 
portion of the 10% Plan allocation made by Mini stries/Departments is credited at the end 
of each financial year in a re serve fund in the Public Acco unt titled ‘Central Resource 
Pool for Development of North Eastern Re gion’ which in administrative parlance is 
known as the Non-Lapsable Cent ral Pool of Resources (NLCPR ).  The funds from this 
Pool are budgeted for financing new infrastruc ture projects/schemes in the region under 
the NLCPR Plan Scheme. 
1.2.4 The broad objective of the NLCPR scheme  is to ensure speedy development of 
infrastructure in the North Eastern Region by increasing the flow of budgetary financing 
for new infrastructure projects/schemes. Both physical and social infrastructure sectors 
are considered for providing support under the Central Pool, with projects in physical 
infrastructure sector receiving priority.  
 
1.2.5 The NLCPR is meant for infrastructure development in almost all the major 
socio-economic development sectors.  For this  purpose, projects are sanctioned for State 
as well as Central sectors.  However, the f unds available under the Central Pool are not 
meant to supplement the normal Plan program mes either of the State Governments or 
Union Ministries/Departments/Agencies.

2.1.10 The Ministry has used the refrain that the main reason for the slow pace of 
utilization of fund is the prolonged monsoon season in the North Eastern Region, which 
severely affects almost all the construction and other economic activities. Besides, the 
 13

Ministry also pleaded that in surgency hampers the utilisatio n of funds.  The expenditure 
normally picks up after the month of Novemb er with a flurry of activities in the 
remaining months of the financial year, i. e., during December-March every year.  The 
Ministry hoped that by the end of financia l year, almost 100% utilisation of allocated 
funds would be achieved. 
 
2.1.11     Human beings have little or no control over the vagaries of weather. 
Likewise, the climatic peculia rities of the North-East are not new and cannot and   
should not be used as a pretext for the sl ow pace of utilization of funds and delayed 
completions of projects in the NER. Theref ore, given the climate conditions of that 
region, it would be a prudent step on the part of administrative Ministry and the 
State Governments, to organize the activities in a rational way to offset the adverse 
impact of the nature. Accordingly, the projects in NER should be implemented 
during the seasons when conditions are favou rable at a grater pace to compensate 
the loss of time during the monsoon season , so that projects are implemented in 
time. In this context, the Committee would li ke to advise the Government to step up 
vigil in monitoring the expenditure as in the flurry of work, there is every likelihood 
of siphoning of funds meant for development.  
 
2.1.12     The Committee is unhappy to note  that only 56.8 % of the allocated fund 
under plan scheme has been utilized upto February end.  The Committee is 
disappointed to note that during the financial year 2008-09, utilization had been low 
in Bodoland Territorial Council (BTC) (6 7%), Advocacy & Publicity (52.8%), 
North Eastern Region Livelihood Projec t (73%) and North Eastern State Road 
Project (Nil). During the financial year upto 28 February, 2010, under utilization of 
funds has been reported in sectors like Non-Lapsable Central Pool of Resources 
(41.1%), North Eastern Council (62.5%), Advocacy & Publicit y (32.5%),  North 
Eastern Region Livelihood Project (19.2%).   The Committee desires to highlight 
that in the case of projects like NERLP, where the vagaries of weather do not play 
any role, only 19.2% of allocated fund has been utilized. That being the case, the 
Committee is not optimistic that the allo cated funds would be fully utilized by 
March 2010. The Committee observes that  under- utilization of funds by the 
Ministry, makes its case weak before the Planning Commission for higher 
projection for allocation.  The Committee fe els that outlays made should give the 
desired results as the Planning Commiss ion would consider the demand for higher 
allocation only when allocated  funds meant for development  of  NE Region are 
fully and optimally utilized and show the results.

2.4 NORTH-EASTERN COUNCIL  
  
2.4.1 The North Eastern Council (NEC) was set up under the NEC Act 1971, to foster 
balanced and integrated economic development of seven constituent member States. By the 
amendment of NEC Act in 2002, Sikkim has been added as its eighth member. It functions as a 
regional planning body for its const ituent States. It is also manda ted to maintain security and 
public order. 
 
 17

2.4.2 The NEC’s role has become more meaningful  when it started receiving funds from the 
Planning Commission for the implementation of th e regional plans.  The Council plays an 
advisory role in areas of interest that are comm on to all its constituent States such as economic 
and social planning, transport, communications, power and flood control. Besides, ensuring 
effective coordination, it is also mandated to put forward proposals for developmental schemes 
and projects submitted by the States to the Centre.  
 
2.4.3 In addition, the NEC provides financial assi stance to member States. The Minister of 
DONER is the Chairman of the NEC. There are two full time nominated Members posted at

3.3.1 The major bottleneck for the development of NER is lack of connectivity, be it 
road, rail or air.     The road connectivity  in the North-East Region is much below as 
compared to the national average.   The Railw ay network in the north -eastern part of the 
country is only 4% of the count ry’s railway network and some of the States of the region 
have zero rail network.  Given the topography and inaccessibility  of the region, air 
transport, more often than not, is the only available mode of transport.

very major problem. The Ministry of Civil Aviation has formed a core committee which 
is trying to sort ou t various connectivity issues in th e NER, with private airlines, Air 
India, etc. The Ministry al so stated that the DGCA has also undertaken a study on 
increasing connectivity with small aircrafts which can be hired or taken on lease by these 
airlines, so that these airports can be revived.

each State, which is the nodal Department fo r NLCPR projects, has been entrusted with

3.5    SARVA SHIKSHA ABHIYAN IN THE REGION 
3.5.1 Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan (SSA ) is Government of India' s flagship programme for 
achievement of Universalization of El ementary Education (UEE) in a time bound 
manner, as mandated by eighty-sixth Amendmen t to the Constitution of India, making 
free and compulsory education to the children of 6-14 years age group, a Fundamental 
Right. The programme seeks to open new schools in those habitations which do not have 
schooling facilities and strengthen existing sc hool infrastructure through provision of 
additional teachers, class rooms, toilets, dr inking water, maintenance grant and school 
improvement grants. SSA has a special focus on girl's education and children with special 
needs. SSA also seeks to provide computer education to bridge the digital divide.  
3.5.2 The North-Eastern States ar e required to meet 10 per cen t of the expenditure from 
their resources as their share for SSA. However,  as per report of th e Thirteenth Finance 
Commission, several of these States have not  been able to provide even this amount, 
leading to slowdown in implementation of SSA.  The Ministry explaining about the status 
stated as under:-  
 “The Ministry of Human Resource De velopment had taken up the case for 
assistance to elementary education sector of NE States by the Thirteenth 
Finance Commission during 2010-2015 to help  these States to fill gaps in 
financing elementary education and en able them to provide their State 
share towards implementation of SSA  programme. Presently, State share 
is outstanding against Arunachal Pradesh, Meghalaya, Mizoram and 
Sikkim. The matter for realizing necessa ry State share has been taken up 
with these States.”  
3.5.3 The Committee observes  that  despit e the literacy rate in the NE region 
standing at 68.5 per cent, with a female literacy rate at 61.5 per cent, which are 
higher than the country’s average of 64.8 per cent and 53.7 per cent, respectively, 
there are significant variations  in the literacy rates am ong different States, with 
Assam, Arunachal Pradesh and Meghalaya below the national average. Moreover, 
there are concerns about the quality of ed ucation. More importantly, the literacy 
rate has not been translated into higher employability or productivity. The 
Committee, therefore, recommends that the Government   should popularize the 
Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan in the region, for equitable outcome of the scheme in all the 
States of the region. 
 
3.5.4 The Committee takes strong exception to  the fact that some of the  North-
Eastern States, namely, Arunachal Prades h, Meghalaya, Mizoram and Sikkim have 
not  provided their 10% share for Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan which has led to 
slowdown in implementation of this fl agship scheme of the Government. The 
Committee recommends that these State Governments should be persuaded to 
 43

provide their share as soon as possible to en able the   implementation of the Scheme 
which is meant to ensure that the fundament al right of the child ren of the country 
becomes a reality. 
3.6    KEY AREAS AND PROJECTS UNDER LOOK EAST POLICY  
3.6.1  The Committee was informed that the "Look East Policy" was launched in 1992 
with the objective of establishing closer ec onomic integration with the Southeast Asian 
countries. The primary objective of the Look Ea st Policy in the context of North Eastern 
Region of India is to take advantage of th e new opportunities in trade and investment by 
improving socio-economic and political relation ship with neighbouring countries.  It was 
a significant shift in India's policy prioritizat ion because hitherto India did not have any 
concrete strategy to create an economic hub in its North Ea stern Region by exploring the 
trade and commerce potential with its ASEAN neighbours. The Committee has also 
learnt that after the releas e of the document “North Ea stern Region Vision 2020” by the 
Prime Minister in July 2008, a serious effo rt has been made for socio-economic 
development of this region to match with the objectives of the Look East Policy. 
3.6.2    The major initiatives under the Look East Policy are as under:   
3.6.3    Kaladan multi-modal project and its implementation 
 The Ministry informed the Committee that the Kaladan Multi-modal Transit 
Transport facility is aimed at establishing connectivity be tween Indian Ports and Sittwe 
Port in Myanmar through riverine transport and road links in Mizoram. The project has 
been approved at a total co st of Rs. 535.91 crore. MEA is  the nodal agency, representing 
Government of India for the project and ha s appointed Inland Wate rways Authority of 
India (IWAI) as Project Development Consultant (PDC). According to the Ministry, 
IWAI has completed the bidding process of aw arding the work for the port at Sittwe and 
Inland Waterways. After assessing the technical specifications and financial bids, IWAI, 
as Project Development Consultant, has ma de recommendation   for awarding work of 
port and IWT component of the Kaladan Multi Modal Transit Transport Project. This is 
being examined by Ministry of External A ffairs. The upgradation of port and waterway 
will span over four years. The actual constr uction of port and IWT terminals at Sittwe 
(Myanmar) and Construction of IWT terminal at Setpyitpyin (Kaletwa, Myanmar) would 
be completed by 2012-13. Construction of ro ad from Kaletwa(Myanmar) to India-
Myanmar border is expected to start from the year 2010-11. The project will be 
completed in three years. 
 
3.6.4 Rih-Tidim and Rih-Falam Road 
 The Committee has been given to understand that in March, 1997 an MoU was 
signed between India and Myanmar on co-ope ration in the devel opment of roads in 
Myanmar along the Indo-Myanmar border  to operationalise the India-Myanmar border 
trading point at Rih-Zokhawthar in Mizoram.  IRCON has consented to study the existing 
DPR and to see the possibility of construc ting the road on the basis of updating the 
existing DPR. IRCON visite d the project site in Myanmar in November, 2009 and 
 44

recommended construction of Rhi-Tiddim road (80 kms approx) first. The cost estimate

 The Committee was informed that India and Bangladesh   has discussed for 
designating Ashuganj as a new Port of Call under Article 23 of the Inland Water Transit

3.8    HYDROPOWER IN THE NORTHEAST: POTENTIAL AND HARNESSING  
  
3.8.1  One of the major assets of the north eastern region is its massive potential of 
hydro-power. Though identified in the early  years after independence, the large 
hydropower potential of the region has remained mostly unexploited so far. Although the 
region has tremendous potential for generating hydroelectric power which is estimated at 
about 60,000 MW, the actual generation is very less.  
  
3.8.2  Regarding progress made to tap the hydr o-power potential available in North East, 
the Ministry has furnished information which is as follows: 
 
“Based on the studies for re-assessment of hydro-electric potential of the 
country, completed by Central Electri city Authority in 1987, assessed 
hydropower potential in the country is about 1,48,701 MW (1,45,320 MW 
for projects with capacity above 25 MW). This includes 62604 MW of 
potential in North Eastern (NE) Region including 4248 MW in the state of 
Sikkim. The assessed potential in NE  Region including Sikkim together 
constitutes about 43% of the total a ssessed hydro power potential in the 
country. Presently, 1.91 % of the assessed potential (for projects above 25 
MW) has already been developed in N. E. region other than Sikkim while 
13.42 % of the assessed potential (for  projects above 25 MW) in Sikkim 
has been developed so far.” 
 
3.8.3 The Ministry further informed that  at present 11 Hydro Electric Projects (above 25 
MW) with an aggregate installed capacity of 1686 MW are in operation in North Eastern 
region and Sikkim.  Besides, 10 H.E. Project s with an aggregate installed capacity of 
4891 MW are under construction both in private a nd public sectors.  In the public sector, 
North Eastern Electric Power Corporat ion (NEEPCO) and National Hydel Power 
Corporation Ltd. (NHPC) are constructing some of the Power Plants.   
 
 47

3.8.4 The Ministry also stated that 141 hydro-electric projects with aggregate capacity of 
57,085 MW have been identified by Central Electricity Authority in North Eastern region 
for implementation and monitoring.  Out of these, 86 projects have been allotted in 
Arunachal Pradesh which includes 74 projects allotted to private sector with aggregate 
capacity of 27512 MW while 4 projects with an aggregate capacity of 5870 MW are 
allotted to CPSUs. In additi on, 8 projects with an aggr egate capacity of 14785 MW are 
yet to be allotted. 
 
3.8.5 The Committee feels that development of hydro electric energy in the region, 
which has vast potential for it, will help make the region as the energy hub.  The 
Committee understands that harnessing  the immense untapped hydropower 
potential in the Northeastern Region will open avenues for growth and provide an 
opportunity to improve the well-being of the people, while making substantial 
contribution to the national economy.  The Committee takes note of the fact that out 
of total potential of about 62604 MW in the region, only 1686 MW has been 
harnessed so far. However, the Committee hopes that with the allotment of various 
projects to private and public sectors, the situation will improve. The necessary road 
and other infrastructure may be put in place so that these projects can be completed 
at the earliest.  
 
3.9   GENERAL RECOMMENDATIONS 
 
(i) The Committee has been given to  understand that there is huge 
potential of agriculture and allied sectors in the North East and 
there is also a huge gap between potential and actual realization. 
In the agriculture and allied sector, investment is low.  The 
Ministry should, therefore, undertak e steps  for ensuring  special 
attention to the agriculture sector.  
 
(ii) A dedicated Small & Medium Enterprises  (SME) Debt Fund is 
needed in the Region to help first time entrepreneurs, which may 
be considered for being set up by SIDBI in association with major 
Banks.  
 
(iii) Reduction in Guarantee Fee (GF)  and Annual Service Fee (ASF) 
from 1.5% to 1% and from 0.75% to 0.5%, respectively, under the 
Credit Guarantee Scheme (CGS) of Credit Guarantee Fund Trust 
For Micro And Small Enterprises (CGTMSE)  is a welcome step. 
But, for NER, CGTMSE may consider further reduction of 50% 
in GF and ASF to make it more effective in the NER. 
 
(iv) Interest Subvention provided in the agriculture sector to 
commercial banks (lending at 7% with the shortfall being made 
up by Government of India) sh ould be widened to include 
development finance institutio n (like NEDFi) not only for 
agricultural credit but also for promoting first generation 
 48

entrepreneurs in the NER for projects upto Rs. 50 lakh. The 
actual lending rate in such cases should be 7% with the deficit 
being made good by the Government of India. 
 
(v) The Government should set up a full fledged technical wing, 
having officers upto the level of Chief Engineer (on deputation 
basis), in the Ministry of DONER to ensure inhouse technical 
competence and expeditious examination of DPRs. 
 
(vi) The Ministry of DoNER and the NEC should engage reputed 
agencies for independent monitoring  of the projects and for DPR 
preparation. The expenses for this purpose should be charged to 
the Scheme concerned (NLCPR and NEC). 
 
 
(vii) A large number of vacancies exist in various Central Government 
organizations in the NER, due to the reluctance of officials to serve 
there on account of difficult conditions in the region. The 
Committee is of the view that th e officials in the Ministry of 
DoNER and Central Government  officials posted in NER 
including those of NEC, shou ld have fixed tenure. The 
Government should provide attrac tive incentives, over and above 
the existing allowances, to th e officials posted in Central 
Government Organizations in the North East. At the same time 
action should be initiated against those officers who do not serve 
or are reluctant to work at the allotted places.  
 
(viii) Suitable training programmes are re quired to be chalked out  in 
IT and ITeS for the youth thro ugh reputed organizations like 
DOEACC. The programmes can be made hugely successful by 
providing employment to the tr ainees in BPOs and similar 
ventures.

OBSERVATIONS/CONCLUSIONS/RECOMMENDATIONS – AT A 
GLANCE 
 
 
IMPLEMENTATION OF NER PROJECTS 
 
Human beings have little or no co ntrol over the vagaries of weather. 
Likewise, the climatic peculia rities of the North-East are not new and cannot and   
should not be used as a pretext for the sl ow pace of utilization of funds and delayed 
completions of projects in the NER. Therefo re, given the climate conditions of that 
region, it would be a prudent step on the part of administrative Ministry and the 
State Governments, to organize the activities in a rational way to offset the adverse 
impact of the nature. Accordingly, the projects in NER should be implemented 
during the seasons when conditions are f avourable at a grater pace to compensate 
the loss of time during the monsoon season , so that projects are implemented in 
time. In this context, the Committee would li ke to advise the Government to step up 
vigil in monitoring the expenditure as in th e flurry of work, there is every likelihood 
of siphoning of funds meant for development.  
(Para 2.1.11) 
 
UNDER UTILIZATION OF FUNDS 
 
The Committee is unhappy to note that only 56.8 % of the allocated fund 
under plan scheme has been utilized upto February end.  The Committee is 
disappointed to note that during the financial year 2008-09, utilization had been low 
in Bodoland Territorial Council (BTC) (6 7%), Advocacy & Publicity (52.8%), 
North Eastern Region Livelihood Projec t (73%) and North Eastern State Road 
Project (Nil). During the financial year upto 28 February, 2010, under utilization of 
funds has been reported in sectors like Non-Lapsable Central Pool of Resources 
(41.1%), North Eastern Council (62.5%), Advocacy & Publicit y (32.5%),  North 
Eastern Region Livelihood Project (19.2%).  The Committee desires to highlight 
that in the case of projects like NERLP, where the vagaries of weather do not play 
any role, only 19.2% of allocated fund has been utilized. That being the case, the 
Committee is not optimistic that the allo cated funds would be fully utilized by 
March 2010. The Committee observes that  under- utilization of funds by the 
Ministry, makes its case weak before the Planning Commission for higher 
projection for allocation.  The Committee fe els that outlays made should give the 
desired results as the Planning Commiss ion would consider the demand for higher 
allocation only when allocated  funds meant for development  of  NE Region are 
fully and optimally utilized and show the results.   
(Para 2.1.12) 
 
TIMELY APPROVAL OF FUNDS BY THE PLANNING COMMISSION 
 
  The Committee is not in agreement with the approach of the Planning 
Commission. The Committee is of the opin ion that the Planning Commission should 
 50

formulate initial projections and give approval thereto. If necessary, those may be

ADVOCACY & PUBLICITY 
 
The Committee takes serious note of the fact that out of Rs. 6.5 crore 
allocated under the Plan Scheme of Advocacy & Publicity during 2008-09, only an 
amount of Rs. 3.54 crore was spent and also during 2009-10, out of Rs. 6 crore only 
Rs. 3 crore were spent till 20-03-2010.  The Committee also takes serious note of the 
reasons for the savings under the scheme in the last two years. Keeping in view the 
trend of under-utilization of the fund meant for this scheme during the previous two 
consecutive years, the Committee apprehe nds repeat of the same outcome in the 
year 2010-11.  The Committee, therefore, st rongly recommends that the Ministry 
should ensure that the measures proposed are actually implemented so that there 
are no unspent balances at the end of the current financial year. The Committee is 
of the view that despite claims of several steps being taken under ‘Advocacy & 
Publicity’ by the Ministry, the results  are still not perceptible. The Committee 
recommends to the Ministry to review its strategy and come out with an innovative 
idea to showcase the Region to the world as an ideal destination for investment, 
tourism etc. 
(Para 2.6.6) 
 
TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE & CAPACITY BUILDING 
  
The  Committee  takes  note  that  th e  allocation  for  the  Scheme of 
Technical Assistance and Capacity Building has been enhanced by 50% in the BE 
2010-11 in comparison to the previous year’s allocation and hopes that it will go a 
long way in developing human resource in  the region.  The Committee also notes 
that the Ministry has tied up with nation al and regional Institutes and centers of 
excellence for imparting professional educat ion to students of the NER.  Vocational 
training and computer training are very important programmes which can improve 
the employment potential for the people of the region. The Committee recommends 
that emphasis may be given on this aspect. 
(Para 2.7.10) 
 
  The Committee expresses serious concern over the inordinate delay in 
setting up the Pilot Training Institute at Lilabari, Assam. The Committee in its One 
Hundred and Thirty Third Report recomme nded for an early decision in starting 
the Institute. Again, the Committee in its One Hundred and Forty First Report 
expressed concern over delay in setting up th e institute. In spit e of this, it is 
unfortunate that the proposal is at land clearance stage though the Committee in its 
One Hundred and Forty First Report     recommended for expediting the process of 
getting land use clearance from Land Advisory Committee, Government of Assam. 
It is surprising and a cause of concern that there is no perceptible change in the 
 52

situation. The Committee strongly recommends that the land clearance issue may be 
sorted out immediately. The Ministry of  Civil Aviation may send its comments 
immediately on the Expression of Interes t (EoI). The Committee desires that the 
Institute should be functional during 2010-11 positively.  
(Para 2.7.11) 
 
EXTERNALLY AIDED PROJECTS   
 
As already mentioned earlier in its One Hundred and Thirty-Third and One 
Hundred and Forty-First Reports, the Committee while expressing its displeasure 
over the sad state of affairs, had recommended for early operationalization of 
externally aided projects like, the NE SRP, NESTICI and NERLP. However, the 
projects have still not moved beyond the drawing board stage. The Committee again 
expresses its displeasure over the fact that the NESRP is still at the Detailed Project 
Reports (DPRs) preparation stage.  The Committee therefore, strongly recommends 
that the Ministry should make sincere effort s in coordination with the Ministry of 
Finance and the external donor agencies to  ensure that the schemes do take off 
during the current financial year. The Committ ee feels that if the projects do not 
take off soon, they may loose the relevance and utility for the NER. 
(Para 2.8.9) 
 
SCHEME UNDER SPECIAL FUND FO R INFRASTRUCTURE UPGRADATION 
IN NORTH EASTERN REGION.  
 
The Committee is happy to note that the scheme under Special Fund for 
Infrastructure upgradation in North Eastern States, is an enabler to identify the 
urgent needs of the North Eastern Region , especially Arunachal Pradesh and the 
border areas and to address their special needs and problems. As this is a good 
opportunity to develop remote areas of NER, th e Committee urges upon the 
Ministry of DoNER to play a pro-active ro le in implementing scheme even though 
this is funded by Ministry of Finance.  
(Para 2.9.4) 
 
NON PLAN LOANS TO NORTH EASTERN HANDICRAFTS AND 
HANDLOOMS DEVELOPMENT CORPORATION (NEHHDC) 
 
The Committee is concerned over the fact that the Corporation is a sick unit 
and has been incurring losses since its inception. Even though the sales are 
increasing, the Corporation is not able to turnaround. The Committee, therefore, 
recommends that the Ministry should unde rtake special steps for financial and 
operational restructuring of the Corporation and make it a viable entity. 
(Para 2.10.6) 
 
LOAN TO NORTH EASTERN REGIONAL AGRICULTURAL MARKETING 
CORPORATION (NERAMAC) 
 
 53

The Committee appreciates that the turn over of the Corporation has almost 
doubled in 2009-10 and it is a positive development.  The Committee desires that the 
Ministry should give further impetus to the development and improvement of 
infrastructure for procurement and market ing of agro-horticultural commodities. 
The Committee feels that as ginger is produced in the region on a massive scale, its 
products need to be taken up for commercialization. The Committee recommends 
that the proposals of setting up Cashew Processing Plant at Mankachar, Assam, 
modernization of Pineapple Juice Plant at Nalkata, Tripur a, setting up Central 
Packaging Centre at Chaigaon in Assam and setting up Multi Fruit Processing 
Plant at Silchar may be implemented at the earliest.  
(Para 2.11.7) 
 
NORTH EASTERN DEVELOPMEN T FINANCE CORPORATION 
LIMITED (NEDFi) 
 
 
The Committee takes note of the activities of NEDFi and its performance and 
hopes that the Corporation will improve it s performance in the years to come so 
that its contribution to the economic growth and development of the region becomes 
significant and noteworthy.  The micro-finance scheme of the Corporation is really 
good and the Committee desires that it may be further strengthened.  
(Para 2.12.8) 
 
 The Committee feels that the government should take further initiatives 
in the field of micro-finance or similar a ssistance to self-help groups, in terms of 
quantum and coverage.  Some beginning   in  this area has already   been made by 
NEDFi. The hill areas are too far from the NEDFi office in Guwahati and the cost of 
servicing these loans is high both for NEDFi and for the loanee. Hence, in the 
remote hill areas, the role of intermediari es like Non-Banking Financial Institutions 
(NBFIs) or NGOs in securing small loans to farmers and small- scale industries is 
crucial. Increasing the number of successful entrepreneurs requires the creation of a 
competitive environment which encourages new entrants and provides enough 
finance for efficient enterprises to expa nd. Appropriate steps are required to be 
taken by the Government in this direction.  
 
(Para 2.12.9) 
 
TRANSFER OF HILL AREA DEV ELOPMENT PROGRAMME (HADP) AND 
BORDER AREA DEVELOPMENT PROGRAMME (BADP) 
 
 
The Committee is exasperated over the fa ct that although three years have 
passed since it made its recommendations, no progress has been made so far and the 
issue is still pending with the Govern ment. The Committee strongly recommends 
that Government should finally arrive at  a decision without further delay in the 
interest of better implementation of the Schemes.  
(Para 3.1.6) 
 54

 
TOURISM  
 
 NE region has great potential to beco me a tourist hot spot in the country 
particularly for eco and adventure to urism. The Committee hopes that the 
initiatives taken including promoting NE brand tourism “Paradise unexplored” 
would go a long way in attracting domestic as well as foreign tourists in the region.  
The Committee desires that the Ministry should prepare a long-term perspective 
plan for developing world class tourism infrastructure in the region. 
(Para 3.2.8) 
 
 The Committee notes that the flow of tourists has increased in Sikkim and 
Arunachal Pradesh due to relaxation of LTC Rules. The Committee would however, 
impresse upon the Government to ensure that  tourists arriving in North East are 
not harassed and exploited by unscrupulous tour operators, travel agents and touts.  
With regard to visit to such places, where permit is required, the Committee 
recommends that procedure for obtaining the same for restricted areas be 
simplified.   
(Para 3.2.9) 
 
CONNECTIVITY 
 
 The Committee feels that development of  infrastructure in the civil aviation 
sector has been hit by bottlenecks main ly on account of land acquisition and 
environmental issues. In this context, th e Committee would like to suggest that a 
Master Plan for creation of civil aviation fac ilities in NE Region on the lines of the 
Road Development Plan namely SARDP-NE may be prepared. In this connection, 
the Committee would like to mention that in  its One Hundred and Thirty-third and 
One Hundred and Forty-first reports, it had recommended for completion of 
upgradation of the airports without furt her delay. The Committee, reiterating its 
earlier recommendations, desires that all necessary steps may be taken for 
development of existing airports and upg radation and operationalisation of non-
operational airports in the NER within a strict time schedule.  
(Para 3.3.17) 
 
 The Committee understands that improvi ng connectivity is the only way to 
develop North Eastern Region and the Govern ment should accord top priority to it. 
The Committee recommends that the Governme nt should expedite all the projects 
on hand for linking the States of the region through rail network.   The target now 
fixed for the completion of the projects is 2016. Though the target  year is far away, 
yet the Committee desires that the Government should stick to this targeted period.  
(Para 3.3.18) 
 
 55

The Committee also recommends that the bottlenecks like  land acquisition, 
environmental clearance, etc. may be remov ed at the earliest so that SARDP-NE 
projects could be completed  as per schedule. 
(Para 3.3.19) 
 
MONITORING MECHANISM 
 
The Committee is of the view that to ma ke any project successful in terms of 
implementation, completion without time a nd cost over-runs, it is imperative to 
have a proper monitoring mechanism. Unfort unately, despite   allocation of large 
amount of funds under various plan schemes,  the region is not only lagging behind 
but the performance of most of the schemes is unsatisfactory which flies in the face 
of the monitoring-mechanism in pl ace. The Committee has repeatedly 
recommended in its earlier reports for  strengthening the monitoring mechanism. 
Reiterating its earlier recommendation , the Committee desires that a robust 
monitoring mechanism may be put in place for ensuring timely completion of the 
projects.  
(Para 3.3.5) 
 
The Committee further recommends that th ere should be a separate wing of 
the Central Vigilance Commission exclusivel y for North Eastern Region to oversee 
proper utilization of public funds for NER projects, from the vigilance angle.  
(Para 3.4.6) 
  
 
The Committee is also of the view that  since huge amount of money is being 
spent on various projects in NE regio n and there is a general feeling of 
misappropriation and siphoning of funds  and that some underground groups are 
also illegally receiving some portion of funds, a post of Joint Director, CBI is 
required to be created for NE Region,  to look into such cases. 
(Para 3.4.7) 
 
The Committee is of the strong view that  the execution of pr ojects should be 
made transparent invariably from the init ial stage of issuance of tender till the 
completion of the projects.  The information relating to name of the projects, its 
cost, time schedule indicating date of  commencement and completion of the 
projects, name of executing agencies and contractors should be displayed at the 
projects sites for the information of the pub lic at large.  The Committee also desires 
that those information may also be posted  on the websites of Ministry of DoNER 
and NEC.   
(Para 3.4.8) 
 
The Committee desires that the Minist ry should ensure that the physical 
outcome must match the financial outlays and that concurrent audit should be 
introduced for release of funds. 
(Para 3.4.9) 
 56

 
SARVA SHIKSHA ABHIYAN IN THE REGION 
 
 The Committee observes  that  despit e the literacy rate in the NE region 
standing at 68.5 per cent, with a female literacy rate at 61.5 per cent, which are 
higher than the country’s average of 64.8 per cent and 53.7 per cent, respectively, 
there are significant variations  in the literacy rates am ong different States, with 
Assam, Arunachal Pradesh and Meghalaya below the national average. Moreover, 
there are concerns about the quality of educ ation. More importantly, the literacy 
rate has not been translated into higher employability or productivity. The 
Committee, therefore, recommends that the Government   should popularize the 
Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan in the region, for equitable outcome of the scheme in all the 
States of the region. 
(Para 3.5.3) 
 
  The Committee takes strong exception to the fact that some of the  North-
Eastern States, namely, Arunachal Prades h, Meghalaya, Mizoram and Sikkim have 
not  provided their 10% share for Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan which has led to 
slowdown in implementation of this fl agship scheme of the Government. The 
Committee recommends that these State Governments should be persuaded to 
provide their share as soon as possible to en able the   implementation of the Scheme 
which is meant to ensure that the fundament al right of the child ren of the country 
becomes a reality. 
(Para 3.5.4) 
 
KEY AREAS AND PROJECTS UNDER LOOK EAST POLICY  
  The Committee understands that the geographical and topographical 
location of the North Eastern States of India joined with the rest of the country by a 
narrow land corridor, of 21 to 40 Km in width and known as the Chicken’s Neck, 
act as a serious impediment for the deve lopment of the region which has resulted 
into the region lagging behind the rest of th e country in terms of infrastructure and 
development. Under the given circumstan ces, massive infrastructural development 
plan is required for all round development of the region.  
(Para 3.6.9) 
 
The Committee is of the considered view  that various road projects linking 
the region with neighbouring landlocked co untries could be of great help in 
increasing border trade with neighboring co untries and tackling insurgency in the 
region. The Committee also feels that the initiatives viz. Kaladan multi-modal 
project, construction of Rih-Tidim and Rih-Falam Road, Ashuganj (Bangladesh) as 
port of call, direct bus service from Kolk ata to Agartala, project on Tri-lateral 
highway connecting Moreh to Maesot (Thailand) via Bagan (Myanmar) and 
improvement of Tamu Kalemyo Kalewa (TKK) Road in Myanmar, etc would 
greatly help opening commercial trade with the neighbouring countries of 
 57

Bangladesh and Myanmar. The Committee,  therefore, recommends that under the 
‘Look East Policy’, the Government may undertake steps towards completion of 
these projects at the earliest. 
(Para 3.6.10) 
 
VISION NER 2020 
 
   The Committee underscores Vision NER 2020 as a guiding document in 
terms of policy formulatio n of action plans and implementation, for overall 
development of the region. The Committee hopes that the Vision Document would 
translate into action plans and invest ments and give the desired results. The 
Committee desires that the Vision Document  would act as catalytic blue-print for 
balanced and equitable development of the region so that the economic growth of 
the North-East Region would catch up with national economic growth.  The 
Committee, therefore,  recommends that development of infrastructure, a sound 
industrial, agricultural and allied sectors with specia l emphasis on horticulture, 
should be given primacy, while implementing the Vision Document.  
 (Para 3.7.3) 
 
   The Committee hopes that Rs. 14 lakh crore, proposed to be invested both 
from public and private sector, as outlined in the document  to enable the region to 
match the National Growth Rate would translate into a reality.  
(Para 3.7.4) 
 
HYDROPOWER IN THE NORTHEAST: POTENTIAL AND HARNESSING  
  
  The Committee feels that development of  hydro electric energy in the region, 
which has vast potential for it, will help make the region as the energy hub.  The 
Committee understands that harnessing  the immense untapped hydropower 
potential in the Northeastern Region will open avenues for growth and provide an 
opportunity to improve the well-being of the people, while making substantial 
contribution to the national economy.  The Committee takes note of the fact that out 
of total potential of about 62604 MW in the region, only 1686 MW has been 
harnessed so far. However, the Committee hopes that with the allotment of various 
projects to private and public sectors, the situation will improve. The necessary road 
and other infrastructure may be put in place so that these projects can be completed 
at the earliest.  
(Para 3.8.5) 
 
GENERAL RECOMMENDATIONS 
 
(ix) The Committee has been given to  understand that there is huge 
potential of agriculture and allied sectors in the North East and 
there is also a huge gap between potential and actual realization. 
In the agriculture and allied sector, investment is low.  The 
 58

Ministry should, therefore, undertak e steps  for ensuring  special 
attention to the agriculture sector.  
 
(x) A dedicated Small & Medium Enterprises  (SME) Debt Fund is 
needed in the Region to help first time entrepreneurs, which may 
be considered for being set up by SIDBI in association with major 
Banks.  
 
(xi) Reduction in Guarantee Fee (GF)  and Annual Service Fee (ASF) 
from 1.5% to 1% and from 0.75% to 0.5%, respectively, under the 
Credit Guarantee Scheme (CGS) of Credit Guarantee Fund Trust 
For Micro And Small Enterprises (CGTMSE)  is a welcome step. 
But, for NER, CGTMSE may consider further reduction of 50% 
in GF and ASF to make it more effective in the NER. 
 
(xii) Interest Subvention provided in the agriculture sector to 
commercial banks (lending at 7% with the shortfall being made 
up by Government of India) sh ould be widened to include 
development finance institutio n (like NEDFi) not only for 
agricultural credit but also for promoting first generation 
entrepreneurs in the NER for projects upto Rs. 50 lakh. The 
actual lending rate in such case s should be 7% with the deficit 
being made good by the Government of India. 
 
(xiii) The Government should set up a full fledged technical wing, 
having officers upto the level of Chief Engineer (on deputation 
basis), in the Ministry of DONER to ensure inhouse technical 
competence and expeditious examination of DPRs. 
 
(xiv) The Ministry of DoNER and the NEC should engage reputed 
agencies for independent monitoring  of the projects and for DPR 
preparation. The expenses for this purpose should be charged to 
the Scheme concerned (NLCPR and NEC). 
 
 
(xv) A large number of vacancies exist in various Central Government 
organizations in the NER, due to the reluctance of officials to serve 
there on account of difficult conditions in the region. The 
Committee is of the view that th e officials in the Ministry of 
DoNER and Central Government  officials posted in NER 
including those of NEC, shou ld have fixed tenure. The 
Government should provide attrac tive incentives, over and above 
the existing allowances, to th e officials posted in Central 
Government Organizations in the North East. At the same time 
action should be initiated against those officers who do not serve 
or are reluctant to work at the allotted places.  
 59

 60
 
(xvi) Suitable training programmes are re quired to be chalked out  in 
IT and ITeS for the youth thro ugh reputed organizations like 
DOEACC. The programmes can be made hugely successful by 
providing employment to the tr ainees in BPOs and similar 
ventures.  
 
(Para 3.9)
